1: # Perfetto - System profiling, app tracing and trace analysis
2: 
3: Perfetto is an open-source suite of SDKs, daemons and tools which use
4: **tracing** to help developers understand the behaviour of complex systems and
5: root-cause functional and performance issues on client and embedded systems.
6: 
7: It is a production-grade tool that is the default tracing system for the
8: **Android operating system** and the **Chromium browser**.
9: 
10: ![](docs/images/perfetto-stack.svg)
11: 
12: ## Core Components
13: 
14: Perfetto is not a single tool, but a collection of components that work
15: together:
16: 
17: - **High-performance tracing daemons:** For capturing tracing information from
18:   many processes on a single machine into a unified trace file.
19: - **Low-overhead tracing SDK:** A C++17 library for direct
20:   userspace-to-userspace tracing of timings and state changes in your
21:   application.
22: - **Extensive OS-level probes:** For capturing system-wide context on Android
23:   and Linux (e.g. scheduling states, CPU frequencies, memory profiling,
24:   callstack sampling).
25: - **Browser-based UI:** A powerful, fully local UI for visualizing and exploring
26:   large, multi-GB traces on a timeline. It works in all major browsers, requires
27:   no installation, and can open traces from other tools.
28: - **SQL-based analysis library:** A powerful engine that allows you to
29:   programmatically query traces using SQL to automate analysis and extract
30:   custom metrics.
31: 
32: ## Why Use Perfetto?
33: 
34: Perfetto was designed to be a versatile and powerful tracing system for a wide
35: range of use cases.
36: 
37: - **For Android App & Platform Developers:** Debug and root-cause functional and
38:   performance issues like slow startups, dropped frames (jank), animation
39:   glitches, low memory kills, and ANRs. Profile both Java/Kotlin and native C++
40:   memory usage with heap dumps and profiles.
41: - **For C/C++ Developers (Linux, macOS, Windows):** Use the
42:   [Tracing SDK](docs/instrumentation/tracing-sdk.md) to instrument your
43:   application with custom trace points to understand its execution flow, find
44:   performance bottlenecks, and debug complex behavior. On Linux, you can also
45:   perform detailed CPU and native heap profiling.
46: - **For Linux Kernel & System Developers:** Get deep insights into kernel
47:   behavior. Perfetto acts as an efficient userspace daemon for `ftrace`,
48:   allowing you to visualize scheduling, syscalls, interrupts, and custom kernel
49:   tracepoints on a timeline.
50: - **For Chromium Developers:** Perfetto is the tracing backend for
51:   `chrome://tracing`. Use it to debug and root-cause issues in the browser, V8,
52:   and Blink.
53: - **For Performance Engineers & SREs:** Analyze and visualize a wide range of
54:   profiling and tracing formats, not just Perfetto's. Use the powerful SQL
55:   interface to programmatically analyze traces from tools like **Linux perf**,
56:   **macOS Instruments**, **Chrome JSON traces**, and more.
57: 
58: ## Getting Started
59: 
60: We've designed our documentation to guide you to the right information as
61: quickly as possible, whether you're a newcomer to performance analysis or an
62: experienced developer.
63: 
64: 1.  **New to tracing?** If you're unfamiliar with concepts like tracing and
65:     profiling, start here:
66: 
67:     - [**What is Tracing?**](https://perfetto.dev/docs/tracing-101) - A gentle
68:       introduction to the world of performance analysis.
69: 
70: 2.  **Ready to dive in?** Our "Getting Started" guide is the main entry point
71:     for all users. It will help you find the right tutorials and documentation
72:     for your specific needs:
73: 
74:     - [**How do I start using Perfetto?**](https://perfetto.dev/docs/getting-started/start-using-perfetto) -
75:       Find your path based on your role and goals (e.g., Android App Developer,
76:       C/C++ Developer, etc.).
77: 
78: 3.  **Want the full overview?** For a comprehensive look at what Perfetto is,
79:     why it's useful, and who uses it, see our main documentation page:
80:     - [**Perfetto Documentation Home**](https://perfetto.dev/docs/)
81: 
82: ## Debian Distribution
83: 
84: For users interested in the Debian distribution of Perfetto, the official source
85: of truth and packaging efforts are maintained at
86: [Debian Perfetto Salsa Repository](https://salsa.debian.org/debian/perfetto)
87: 
88: ## Community & Support
89: 
90: Have questions? Need help?
91: 
92: - **[GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/google/perfetto/discussions/categories/q-a):**
93:   For Q&A and general discussions.
94: - **[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/google/perfetto/issues):** For bug
95:   reports.
96: - **[Discord](https://discord.gg/35ShE3A):** For live chat with the community
97:   and developers.
98: 
99: We follow
100: [Google's Open Source Community Guidelines](https://opensource.google/conduct/).

range of use cases.

## Immediate Subdirectories under `D:\PC-LIB_ANALYSIS\repos\pc-lib-3456\perfetto\src\`

| Directory | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `android_internal` | Android-internal tracing probes — HAL bindings for atrace, power stats, incident service, statsd, suspend control, etc. |
| `android_sdk` | Android SDK surface for Perfetto — Java/JNI bindings and `nativehelper`. |
| `android_stats` | Android-specific statsd logging helpers (`statsd_logging_helper`). |
| `base` | Core base library — platform abstractions (threading, file I/O, string utilities, UUID, logging, event-fd, Unix sockets, HTTP, regex, etc.). |
| `bigtrace` | Bigtrace orchestrator + worker for large-scale trace processing pipelines. |
| `ipc` | Inter-process communication transport layer (Unix-domain socket based, used by `traced` ↔ client). |
| `java_sdk` | Java SDK layer (separate from `android_sdk`; general Java API surface). |
| `kallsyms` | Kernel symbol resolution — parses `/proc/kallsyms` for symbolizing kernel addresses in traces. |
| `kernel_utils` | Kernel utility helpers — syscall table, wakelock error definitions. |
| `perfetto_cmd` | The main `perfetto` CLI tool — trace config parsing, trigger, packet writer, plus an Android-specific variant. |
| `profiling` | Process profiling — `memory/` (heapprofd, client hooks), `perf/` (perf-event-based CPU profiling), `common/`, `smaps/`. |
| `protovm` | ProtoVM — a lightweight custom VM for efficient protobuf processing on trace data (includes compiler + executor). |
| `protozero` | ProtoZero — zero-copy protobuf serialization/deserialization library (core of Perfetto's wire format). Subdirs: `filtering/`, `protoc_plugin/`, `text_to_proto/`, `descriptor_diff/`. |
| `proto_utils` | Protobuf utility tools — pb↔text conversion, WASM build target. |
| `shared_lib` | Shared library C API SDK — a stable C ABI surface for embedding Perfetto tracing into arbitrary processes (headers, `track_event` wrappers). |
| `tools` | Standalone tools — `busy_threads/`, `cpu_utilization/`, `dump_ftrace_stats/`, `ftrace_proto_gen/`, `protoprofile/`, `proto_filter/`, `proto_merger/`, `skippy/`, `string_filter_tool/`, plus `idle_alloc`, `multithreaded_alloc`, profiling sample distribution, tracing proto extensions. |
| `tracebox` | `tracebox` — a tracing sandbox/isolator executable. |
| `traceconv` | `traceconv` — trace format converter (JSON, systrace, Firefox profiler, pprof, text). |
| `traced` | The `traced` service daemon — `probes/` (ftrace, /proc pollers, etc.) + `service/` (producer/consumer broker). |
| `traced_relay` | `traced_relay` — socket relay service for remote/forwarded tracing. |
| `trace_processor` | The trace processor engine — SQLite-backed query engine with `core/`, `importers/` (systrace/ftrace/proto/track-event), `metrics/`, `perfetto_sql/`, `plugins/`, `rpc/`, `shell/`, `sorter/`, `sqlite/`, `storage/`, `tables/`, `trace_summary/`, `types/`, `util/`. |
| `trace_redaction` | Trace redaction / PII scrubbing pipeline — clock conversion, ftrace/sched/process event redaction, frame cookies, package list pruning, integrity verification. |
| `tracing` | Core tracing engine — SDK-side API (`tracing.cc`, `data_source.cc`, `track_event_*`), IPC client bindings (`ipc/`), service stubs (`service/`, `core/`), plus platform backends (`platform_posix.cc`, `platform_windows.cc`). |
| `websocket_bridge` | WebSocket bridge — exposes a tracing interface to browser-based clients via WebSocket. |

project(
    'perfetto',
    ['cpp'],

fs = import('fs')

if not fs.is_dir('sdk')
    error('sdk dir not found, please checkout a release tag, e.g. v14.0')
endif

cpp = meson.get_compiler('cpp')

deps_perfetto = [dependency('threads')]

if host_machine.system() == 'android'
  deps_perfetto += cpp.find_library('log')
endif

lib_perfetto = static_library(
    'perfetto',
    sources: 'sdk/perfetto.cc',
    dependencies: deps_perfetto,
    install: true,
    cpp_args: '-std=c++17',
)

dir_perfetto_trace = join_paths(meson.current_source_dir(),

install_data(dir_perfetto_trace / 'perfetto_trace.proto')

dep_perfetto = declare_dependency(
    link_with: lib_perfetto,
    include_directories: inc_perfetto,
    variables: {
        'pkgdatadir': dir_perfetto_trace,
    }

def _to_array(value):
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return value
    if value is None or value == "":
        return []
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        # A *wrapper* object groups items under one or more list-of-objects props
        # (e.g. entry_points {primary_entry_points:[{…},…], startup_type:"…"}) →
        # flatten those object-lists into the item array, dropping scalar metadata.
        # A single item object whose only list is a scalar field (e.g. its own
        # evidence:[str,…]) has no object-list → wrap the whole object as one item.
        groups = [v for v in value.values()
                  if isinstance(v, list) and any(isinstance(el, dict) for el in v)]
        if groups:
            flat = []
            for v in groups:
                flat.extend(v)
            return flat
        return [value]
    return [value]


def _to_string(value):
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return "；".join(_to_string(v) for v in value if v not in (None, ""))
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return "；".join(f"{k}: {_to_string(v)}" for k, v in value.items())
    return str(value)


def coerce_to_schema(value, schema, path, fixes):
    """Recursively normalise `value` to the shape `schema` declares, appending a
    {path, from, to} record to `fixes` for each coercion. Returns the (possibly
    new) value; mutates dicts/lists in place where no type change is needed."""
    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
        return value
    schema = _resolve_ref(schema)
    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
        return value
    if any(k in schema for k in ("oneOf", "anyOf", "allOf")):
        return value  # a choice — don't guess which branch was intended

    types = _schema_types(schema)

    # No explicit type: only descend when the container shape already matches.
    if types is None:
        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(schema.get("properties"), dict):
            return _recurse_object(value, schema, path, fixes)
        if isinstance(value, list) and isinstance(schema.get("items"), dict):
            return [coerce_to_schema(v, schema["items"], f"{path}[{i}]", fixes)
                    for i, v in enumerate(value)]
        return value

    if value is None:
        return value  # never fabricate a value for null

    actual = _typename(value)
    if actual in types or (actual == "integer" and "number" in types):
        # already conformant → recurse into structure to fix nested fields
        if actual == "object" and isinstance(schema.get("properties"), dict):
            return _recurse_object(value, schema, path, fixes)
        if actual == "array" and isinstance(schema.get("items"), dict):
            return [coerce_to_schema(v, schema["items"], f"{path}[{i}]", fixes)
                    for i, v in enumerate(value)]
        return value

    # mismatch → coerce toward a concrete target we can build safely
    if "array" in types:
        new = _to_array(value)
        fixes.append({"path": path or "$", "from": actual, "to": "array"})
        items = schema.get("items")

        return new
    if "string" in types:
        fixes.append({"path": path or "$", "from": actual, "to": "string"})
        return _to_string(value)
    # object/number/int/bool targets: no safe reconstruction from a wrong type → leave as-is
    return value
